newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-CECIL, SHEIKH MOHAMMED IN RECONCILIATION.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CECIL, SHEIKH MOHAMMED IN RECONCILIATION.

text.p: Top filly Bosra Sham won the Champion Stakes on Saturday, virtually clinching the 1996 trainers' title for Henry Cecil and effecting a reconcilation between Cecil and Dubai's Sheikh Mohammed.

The two men have not spoken to each other for some considerable time after splitting in acrimonious circumstances last year over the training of Mark of Esteem who has proved this season to be Europe's top miler.

On Saturday, Bosra Sham (9-4), ridden by Pat Eddery, sprinted two and a half lengths clear of even money favourite Halling, trained for the sheikh's Godolphin operation by Saeed bin Suroor, to lift the $276,000 top prize for owner Wafic Said.
Ironically, the group one race, known in full as the Dubai Champion Stakes, was sponsored by Sheik Mohammed and his family, so it was the sheikh who made the presentation to Cecil as winning trainer.
Shaking him warmly by the hand, the sheikh said: "Congratulations. That was your hard work. Good luck."
Then, in mock theatre, he jokingly turned Cecil's prize, a silver dagger for opening envelopes, on himself as if the trainer was stabbing him in the heart.
"That is the first time we have talked for a long time," said Cecil afterwards. "He behaved like a gentleman. He couldn't have been nicer. I would like to think we are friends. We are not enemies."
It had been a dazzling performance by the 1,000 Guineas winnner Bosra Sham, who has suffered during the season from a foot problem which has restricted her racecourse appearances.
Cecil, who now looks assured of his 11th title with three weeks of the season left, was near to tears as the filly made her way back to the unsaddling enclosure.
He now enjoys a lead of around 56,000 pounds ($89,000) over bin Suroor, his big rival.

Cecil's rift last year with the sheikh left observers to wonder whether he could ever be champion again without his leading patron. But the Newmarket handler has struck back in the most eloquent way and his winnings for the season now stand at around 1.86 million pounds ($2.95 million).
Only six contested the race but it was a quality affair with Halling bidding to add the Champion Stakes to earlier group one victories in the York International and Sandown Eclipse Stakes.
Winning jockey Eddery said :"It was just great."Cecil said: "She is definitely in the same league as Indian Skimmer and Oh So Sharp. They are the three best fillies I have ever seen."

It was the first defeat on grass in 13 starts for Halling, ridden on Saturday by Frankie Dettori. Godolphin racing manager Simon Crisford said: "With five group one successes, Halling has been a fantastic flag-bearer, a wonderfully tough courageous horse. No decision has been made but it may be that he will be retired."
Timarida, the Irish Champion Stakes winner, finished a good third ahead of Even Top and Royal Ascot winner First Island.
